hilfe: Processing: turning one state into another.
This is NOT a fixed chain, it is a NET. Several steps can lead out of one
state, and one step can start from several states. That is exactly where
the decision comes from: which way do you take?
reinheit.start   Purity in percent that a freshly mined block carries into
your bag. An ore may set its own value in data/erze.json
with "reinheit": 65.
reinheit.wert_min / wert_max
What purity does to the price: at 0% wert_min counts, at
100% wert_max, linear in between.
zustandswert     Factor on the base value of the ore, per state. It only
depends on the state, never on the way there - so two ways
to the same state give the same price.
Price of one piece = wert (from erze.json) * zustandswert * purity factor
* money per block (from the skill tree).
One line in "schritte":
befehl    what it is called in player code: item.wash("Gold").
Possible are wash, smelt, cast, clean, polish, harden,
refine, press - each one has its own point in the skill tree.
name      what the bag menu shows.
von       LIST of states this step can start from.
zu        what comes out of it.
dauer     seconds per piece. Only ONE job runs at a time.
reinheit  change in percentage points, may be negative. The result is
clamped to 0..100.
A step only works if the ore allows the target state in its own list
"zustaende" - you do not melt a diamond.
"oxidized" and "alloy" have no step on purpose: alloying comes later,
oxidizing is decay.
"etched" and "fused" are the end of the chain. They are deliberately
slow and expensive: late in the game a stack should get DEEPER, not just
wider. Etching even costs purity - so it only pays off on something you
have already cleaned up properly.
